doc.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Basie nicknames and Lester Young's school bell
summary: Joe Williams came after his tenure; Lester Young called Basie Holy Man, later called The Chief, and rang a school bell at new players who did not swing.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Wow. That’s wonderful. Before we wrap up is there any—
It’s on its way. Is there any humorous or just really interesting stories you can share with us about either Basie or Joe Williams, the time together, that maybe we haven’t read in a book.
Well there’s not too much I could say about Joe because he wasn’t with the band that I was with. I was with the original Count Basie band.
His hit came after your tenure — that “Every Day.”

Oh, yeah. That’s after I had left the band in the 50’s. And Lester Young gave Basie the name of “Holy Man” because he carried the money. He was the “Holy Man.” And we had to keep track of Basie so we could get paid. ‘Cause he’d find a bar someplace and we wouldn’t get any money. We didn’t get no dough. It was so much fun you know. So many stories I could tell but you couldn’t present them to the school, the stories.
Have to clean them up a little bit, huh?
Where did he get the name “The Chief?” Do you remember that?
Well that was after I left the band.
It was “The Count” until a certain time when he became “The Chief.”

He was the “Holy Man.” He was the “Holy Man” and then the late band with Joe Williams and all of them, they called him “The Chief.” See but before then, Lester Young named him “Holy Man.” So everybody had a name. Lester gave everybody a name. And he was so full of humor. If someone new would come in the band, he had a little school bell that he’d put down beside him and if you didn’t play the way that you should, I mean swing and everything, he’d take the bell and ring it. And Basie would give you a notice.
Yeah. It was a lot of fun, though. It was a lot of fun.
